candidates.attacker_control: Any HTTP client controls the JMSDestination query parameter, which ApplicationContextFilter binds directly onto the request-scoped messageQuery bean (DestinationFacade.setJMSDestination trims only); the same parameter also reaches queueConsumerQuery/queueBrowseQuery. Any JMS client controls its clientId and connection id (ConnectionInfo), which flow into JMSMessageID and into the consumer/message views; broker authentication is not required to inject these strings (only to view the console as a victim).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked sibling output sinks and tag files: queues.jsp escapes QueueFilter via <c:out>; graph.jsp escapes the same JMSMessageID field; connections/queueProducers/queueGraph/xml views escape; tooltip.tag replaces < and >, short.tag HTML+JS-escapes, escape.tag URL-encodes; c:out-wrapped values exist in the same rows as the cited raw sinks. Verified the script block is outside the c:choose so it renders even when no message is found, and verified web.xml maps ApplicationContextFilter to /* so requestContext is populated for direct JSP requests. Counterweight: the shipped console requires BASIC auth for *.jsp, so exploitation needs a victim (reflected) or a persisted bad value plus an operator viewing the page (stored); nothing in source indicates runtime blocking.
candidates.impact: Attacker JavaScript executes in the web console origin under the victim's authenticated session: it can read the per-session XSRF 'secret' rendered into console pages and call console actions (delete/purge/retry destinations and messages, send messages) or exfiltrate broker data. The stored variants persist (until the client disconnects or the message is removed) and trigger whenever an operator views the affected page.
candidates.prerequisites: Web console deployed and reachable (standard distribution exposes it via Jetty; assembly/src/release/conf/jetty.xml constrains *.jsp and /admin/* behind BASIC auth). For the reflected variant, an authenticated console user must open a crafted message.jsp?JMSDestination=...</script><script>... URL (the script block at lines 228-242 is emitted unconditionally, outside the empty-message c:choose). For the stored variants, an authenticated user must view queueConsumers.jsp for a queue where an attacker client is attached, or browse a queue containing the attacker-influenced message id.
candidates.root_cause: The web console binds raw HTTP request parameters onto request-scoped query beans (ApplicationContextFilter.createRequestContextWrapper uses ServletRequestDataBinder; DestinationFacade.setJMSDestination only trims) and then interpolates those values, and broker/client-controlled strings, directly into JSP output. message.jsp emits ${requestContext.messageQuery.JMSDestination} and ${row.JMSMessageID} inside an inline <script> block without JS/HTML encoding; queueConsumers.jsp emits ${row.clientId} raw in HTML text; browse.jsp emits ${row.JMSMessageID} raw in link text. Sibling rows/attributes in the same files use <c:out>, and the xml/*.jsp views and tag files escape, so the missing encoding in these sinks is an oversight, not a deliberate policy.
candidates.title: Unescaped web-console output allows reflected/stored XSS in ActiveMQ Web Console (message.jsp / queueConsumers.jsp / browse.jsp)
candidates.trace: HTTP GET /admin/message.jsp?JMSDestination=<payload> -> ApplicationContextFilter.doFilter (activemq-web-console/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/web/filter/ApplicationContextFilter.java:82-102,166-199) sets the requestContext wrapper and binds request parameters onto the request-scoped messageQuery bean (activemq-web-console/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/webconsole-query.xml:22) -> MessageQuery extends DestinationFacade; setJMSDestination only trims (activemq-web/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/web/DestinationFacade.java:86-95) -> message.jsp:238 concatenates the raw value into the inline script's url variable (line 239 does the same with ${row.JMSMessageID}); queueConsumers.jsp:65 and browse.jsp:53 render clientId/JMSMessageID raw in HTML context.
candidates.unverified: No runtime reproduction; JSP/tag rendering and Jetty auth behavior were not executed. The precise sink addressed by the corresponding historical web-console XSS fix cannot be confirmed from this snapshot alone, so three related sinks of the same missing-encoding root cause are cited. The stored variants additionally depend on the broker accepting arbitrary client-supplied clientId/connection id strings, which was inferred from ConnectionInfo handling but not runtime-verified.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-Site Scripting')

coverage_summary: Scope from get_source_scope: 2691 files at the source root, binaries skipped by content probe; all readable files were in scope, none excluded as sensitive or over size. Relation index coverage from get_relation_scope: partial, 2623/2691 files indexed (68 files absent), 2292 Java files, 35k symbols/90k call sites, 54392 unresolved calls, no control-flow or data-flow analysis, no semantic resolution, Spring annotations name-based only; index labels were treated as navigation hints and every cited edge was verified in source text. Deep reads: activemq-web-console JSPs, tag files, ApplicationContextFilter, web.xml, webconsole-query.xml, jetty.xml constraints; activemq-web DestinationFacade/MessageQuery; OpenWire codec stack (OpenWireFormat.unmarshal/doUnmarshal, ExceptionResponseMarshaller, BaseDataStreamMarshaller v1/v9-v12 and openwire-legacy versions); TcpTransport read path; broker security package (AuthorizationBroker, SimpleAuthenticationBroker, SecurityContext); JAAS LDAPLoginModule; assembly default activemq.xml transport connectors. Spot checks: AMQP/STOMP/MQTT wire formats, JDBC store statements, JMX AnnotatedMBean. Not exhaustively read: ~2600 remaining files (unit tests, console/tooling, camel/karaf/osgi modules, leveldb store), and JSP rendering semantics were reasoned statically only.
limitations: No code was executed, built, or tested; no scanner or dynamic confirmation was performed, so all findings are static leads rather than confirmed vulnerabilities.

The relation index is partial (68 files absent) and implements no control-flow/data-flow or semantic resolution; absence of an indexed relation never proves absence of a path, and index labels were not treated as verdicts.

The web-console candidate identifies a cluster of unescaped sinks sharing one missing-encoding root cause; the specific sink tied to the historical console XSS fix cannot be pinned down from this snapshot, and no CVE/patch metadata was consulted.

Exploitability preconditions (Jetty BASIC auth for *.jsp, operator viewing affected pages, broker acceptance of arbitrary clientId/connection id, actual LDAP server bind semantics) were inferred from source and config, not verified at runtime.

The OpenWire throwable-instantiation lead was verified only at source level (control flow to createThrowable and gadget availability in the assembly descriptors); runtime reachability/gadget success was not tested.

rejected_leads.lead: OpenWire ExceptionResponse throwable instantiation: BaseDataStreamMarshaller.createThrowable does Class.forName(attacker-controlled name, false, ...) then clazz.getConstructor(String.class).newInstance(attacker message) and only afterwards casts to Throwable (activemq-client/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/openwire/v12/BaseDataStreamMarshaller.java:227-232; same code in v1/v9/v10/v11 and openwire-legacy v2-v8; reached via ExceptionResponseMarshaller unmarshal lines 109-115/65-71 and OpenWireFormat.doUnmarshal/TcpTransport.readCommand before any broker authentication; default distribution ships spring-context so a String-constructor gadget is on the classpath).
rejected_leads.reason: Genuine, separate and potentially higher-impact root cause, but not selected because only one candidate is allowed for this review and the web-console cluster was chosen as the case-focused lead. Listed here for follow-up verification; not runtime-confirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: LDAPLoginModule user bind with an empty password: authenticate() maps a missing password callback to "" (activemq-jaas/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/jaas/LDAPLoginModule.java:123-136) and bindUser() sets SECURITY_CREDENTIALS to that empty value and treats a successful getAttributes() as a valid bind (lines 437-470), which some LDAP servers treat as an anonymous bind; LDAPAuthorizationMap/LDAPLoginModule configured-credential checks exist but user-password emptiness is not rejected.
rejected_leads.reason: Config-dependent authentication-bypass lead; impact and reachability depend on the LDAP server's anonymous-bind policy and JAAS configuration that this snapshot does not pin down, so it was not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: SubQueueSelectorCacheBroker reads its selector cache with a plain ObjectInputStream from a persisted file (activemq-broker/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/plugin/SubQueueSelectorCacheBroker.java:193-200).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires local filesystem write access to the configured persistence file; no remote attacker control found, so below the evidence/impact threshold.
The map is populated as destination->destination, and ActiveMQDestination.equals/hashCode are consistent, so containsValue and containsKey are equivalent here; no authorization bypass identified.

summary: Reviewed the assigned snapshot of Apache ActiveMQ 5.15.12 (2691 source files; 2292 Java files across activemq-client/broker/web/web-console/jaas/transports/stores, plus JSP/XML/config). The selected candidate is a web-console output-encoding cluster: request-bound JMSDestination and broker/client-controlled clientId / JMSMessageID are written into JSP HTML/JavaScript without encoding, giving reflected and stored XSS in the authenticated console origin. Secondary leads found but not submitted under the one-candidate cap are listed in rejected_leads, most notably the OpenWire ExceptionResponse throwable instantiation path (createThrowable: Class.forName on a wire-supplied class name + single-String constructor newInstance, in v1/v9–v12 and legacy marshallers), which is reachable from TcpTransport.readCommand before broker authentication and is a separate, higher-impact root cause that deserves follow-up. No runtime confirmation was performed; all statements are static source evidence.
